description:
Files:
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/lib.rs:24-29 (six `pub mod` declarations)
- crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/mod.rs:8-15, 1287-1289 (ten sub-modules)

`lib.rs` declares:
```rust
pub mod methods;
pub mod session;
pub mod sse;
pub mod types;
pub mod utils;
pub mod ws;
```

And `methods/mod.rs` declares ten `pub mod` sub-modules (`blob`, `chat`, `contact`, `custom_emoji`, `message`, `misc`, `quota`, `space`, `space_ban`, `space_invite`).

Combined with the explicit `pub use methods::{...}` re-exports in `lib.rs:32-45`, callers can reach the same type via two paths:

- `jmap_chat_client::Quota`
- `jmap_chat_client::methods::quota::Quota`

Same for `ChatSseEvent` (root re-export + `sse::ChatSseEvent`), `ChatWsExt` (root + `ws::ChatWsExt`), `ChatCapability` (root + `session::ChatCapability`), every input/patch struct, etc.

Caller impact:
- The crate has implicitly committed to both paths. A future refactor that renames `methods::quota` to `methods::quotas` or moves the `Quota` struct into `methods/mod.rs` directly breaks every consumer who imports the inner path.
- IDE auto-import can pick the inner path arbitrarily, leading to inconsistent imports across a downstream codebase.
- `cargo public-api` diffs treat the two paths as distinct items, doubling the surface area shown.

Examination of the modules:
- `types` and `utils` — the *only* path: `types::BodyType` etc. and `utils::format_receipt_timestamp` are not re-exported at the root. So `pub mod` is necessary here. Consider re-exporting at the root too (matches the convention of every other module), or commit to the inner path as canonical.
- `methods`, `session`, `sse`, `ws` — fully duplicated by root re-exports. `pub mod` adds nothing for the consumer; consider `pub(crate) mod`.
- The ten `methods::*` sub-modules — same: every public item is re-exported through `methods/mod.rs::pub use ...`. `pub(crate)` would not regress reachability via the crate root, only eliminate the inner path.

Fix paths:
1. **Tighten visibility**: change `pub mod methods`, `pub mod session`, `pub mod sse`, `pub mod ws` to `pub(crate)`. Re-export `types` and `utils` items at root and tighten those too. Net change: single canonical path for every item.
2. **Document both paths as committed**: add a crate-level rustdoc note "all public items are accessible from both the crate root and their defining module; both paths are stable." Then maintenance cost is real and visible.

Option 1 is cleaner. Option 2 is honest about current state.

The same pattern likely affects every other `*-client` and `*-server` crate in the workspace per canonical-template propagation. A workspace-wide decision is needed before this can be acted on.
title: pub mod granularity creates dual paths for every re-exported item
